library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)

## Literature / Publications

### Key References

1.  **Pimm et al. 1995. Science.** [The Future of Biodiversity](https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.269.5222.347)
    -   E/MSY source
    -   Established the methodology for calculating extinction rates using the E/MSY metric and proposed the widely cited baseline background rate of 1 E/MSY
2.  **Barnosky et al. 2011. Nature.** [Has the Earth's sixth mass extinction already arrived?](https://www.nature.com/articles/nature09678)
    -   Table 2: Methods of comparing present and past extinctions
    -   Compare currently measured extinction rates to background rates assessed from fossil record with E/MSY
    -   Section: Background rate comparisons
        -   "A useful and widely applied metric has been E/MSY (extinctions per million species-years, as defined in refs 15 and 27). In this approach, background rates are estimated from fossil extinctions that took place in million-year-or-more time bins. For current rates, the proportion of species extinct in a comparatively very short time (one to a few centuries) is extrapolated to predict what the rate would be over a million years."
3.  **Pimm et al. 2014. Science.** [The biodiversity of species and their rates of extinction, distribution, and protection](https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.1246752)
    -   Uses E/MSY for current rate
4.  **Ceballos et al. 2015. Science.** [Accelerated modern human--induced species losses: Entering the sixth mass extinction](https://www.science.org/doi/epdf/10.1126/sciadv.1400253)
    -   Uses E/MSY for current rate

## E/MSY (Extinctions per Million Species-Years)

**E/MSY** is a standardized metric used to quantify and compare extinction rates across different time periods and taxonomic groups.

**Formula:**

```         
E/MSY = (Number of extinctions / (Number of species at risk × Time period in years)) × 1,000,000
```

## E/MSY for Hawaiian Asteraceae

Input data

```{r}
# Hawaiian Asteraceae data
total_species <- 101
extinctions <- 12
years <- 2026 - 1778  # 248 years since European arrival

# Background rates
background_rate_max_age_6.15myr <- 0.97    # Max Age - 6.15myr
background_rate_precise_6.15myr <- 0.80    # Precise - 6.15myr

data.frame(
  Parameter = c("Total species", "Extinctions", "Years elapsed", "Max Age - 6.15myr background", "Precise - 6.15myr background"),
  Value = c(total_species, extinctions, years, background_rate_max_age_6.15myr, background_rate_precise_6.15myr)
) %>% 
  kable(caption = "Hawaiian Asteraceae Analysis Parameters", digits = 2) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed")) %>%
  column_spec(1, bold = TRUE)
```

### Calculate Current Extinction Rate (Linear)

```{r}
# Calculate current extinction rate
extinction_rate <- extinctions / (total_species * years)
extinctions_per_million_species_years <- extinction_rate * 1000000

# Current extinction rate:
round(extinctions_per_million_species_years,1)
```

Breakdown

```         
E/MSY = (12 extinctions / (101 species × 248 years)) × 1,000,000
= (12 / 25,048) × 1,000,000
= 0.0004790802 × 1,000,000
= 479.1 E/MSY
```

### Calculate Current Extinction Rate (exponential)

Although E/MSY is typically calculated using a discrete formulation (observed extinctions / species-years), extinction in continuous time follows an exponential decay process. For comparison, we additionally calculate the *instantaneous* modern extinction rate, which treats the loss of 10 species over 247 years as a single exponential decline.

This instantaneous rate represents the per-species hazard (μ) that would produce the observed proportion of species remaining, assuming continuous exponential decay:

```         
μ = -ln(S_after / S_before) / time
```

The resulting μ can then be expressed in E/MSY units by multiplying by 1,000,000.

```{r}
## Instantaneous (exponential) modern extinction rate
## Using exponential decay: mu = -ln(S_after / S_before) / t

S_before <- total_species
S_after  <- total_species - extinctions

# instantaneous annual extinction hazard (per species per year)
mu_instantaneous <- -log(S_after / S_before) / years

# convert instantaneous hazard to E/MSY (mu × 1,000,000)
instantaneous_emsy <- mu_instantaneous * 1000000

# Show instantaneous E/MSY
round(instantaneous_emsy, 1)

```

Using exponential decay:

$$
\mu = -\ln\left(\frac{S_{\text{after}}}{S_{\text{before}}}\right) / t
$$

Where:\
- $S_{\text{before}} = 101$\
- $S_{\text{after}} = 89$\
- $t = 248 \text{ years}$

Breakdown:

```         
Instantaneous μ = -ln(89 / 101) / 248
                = -ln(0.881188) / 248
                = 0.12647 / 248
                = 0.00050996 per species-year

Instantaneous E/MSY = 0.00050996 × 1,000,000
                    = 509.96 E/MSY
```

This value is slightly higher than the discrete estimate (\~479.1 E/MSY), as expected under exponential decay.

### Compare Current Extinction Rate to Background Rates

Calculate rate increases:

Linear

```{r}
rate_increase_max_age <- extinctions_per_million_species_years / background_rate_max_age_6.15myr
rate_increase_precise <- extinctions_per_million_species_years / background_rate_precise_6.15myr
```

Exponential

```{r}
# Ratio: instantaneous E/MSY divided by background E/MSY (same as other ratio calculation)
rate_increase_instant_max_age <- instantaneous_emsy / background_rate_max_age_6.15myr
rate_increase_instant_precise  <- instantaneous_emsy / background_rate_precise_6.15myr
```

Comparison table

```{r}
comparison_table <- data.frame(
  Background_Model = c("Max Age - 6.15myr", "Precise - 6.15myr"),
  Background_Rate = c(background_rate_max_age_6.15myr, background_rate_precise_6.15myr),
  Current_Rate = rep(round(extinctions_per_million_species_years, 1), 2),
  Instantaneous_Current_Rate = rep(round(instantaneous_emsy, 1), 2),
  Rate_Increase = c(round(rate_increase_max_age, 0), round(rate_increase_precise, 0)),
  Instantaneous_Rate_Increase = c(round(rate_increase_instant_max_age, 0), round(rate_increase_instant_precise, 0))
)

kable(comparison_table, caption = "Rate Comparison: Current vs Background") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
                full_width = FALSE, position = "center") %>%
  column_spec(1, bold = TRUE) %>%
  column_spec(5:6, bold = TRUE, color = "red")
```

## Comparing Modern to Natural (DAISIE) Extinctions

**Methodological Considerations**

Both metrics represent extinction risk per species per unit time, but are scaled differently:

-   DAISIE: Continuous-time rate (instantaneous risk)

-   Modern E/MSY: Discrete-time average (observed extinctions over a fixed period)

The difference is probably negligible for comparison purposes. To properly compare, we need to translate the DAISIE extinction rate into expected number of extinctions over our 247-year study period.

### Expected Extinctions Calculation

```{r}
# Expected extinctions = N × μ × t 
# N = Number of species at risk (101)
# μ = Annual extinction rate (converted from DAISIE background rates)
# t = Time period in years (248 years since European arrival)

# Convert E/MSY to annual rates (DAISIE translation)
annual_rate_max_age <- background_rate_max_age_6.15myr / 1000000
annual_rate_precise <- background_rate_precise_6.15myr / 1000000

# Calculate expected extinctions under background rates
expected_max_age <- total_species * annual_rate_max_age * years
expected_precise <- total_species * annual_rate_precise * years

```

```{r}
# Show the translation calculations
translation_calc <- data.frame(
  Model = c("Max Age - 6.15myr", "Precise - 6.15myr"),
  DAISIE_Rate = c(background_rate_max_age_6.15myr, background_rate_precise_6.15myr),
  Annual_Rate = c(annual_rate_max_age, annual_rate_precise),
  Calculation = c(
    paste0(total_species, " × ", format(annual_rate_max_age, scientific = TRUE), " × ", years),
    paste0(total_species, " × ", format(annual_rate_precise, scientific = TRUE), " × ", years)
  ),
  Expected_Extinctions = c(round(expected_max_age, 5), round(expected_precise, 5))
)

kable(translation_calc, caption = "DAISIE Rate Translation: From E/MSY to Expected Extinctions") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
                full_width = FALSE, position = "center") %>%
  column_spec(1, bold = TRUE)
```

Compare expected (DAISIE background) to observed number of extinctions since 1778

```{r}
expected_extinctions <- data.frame(
  Model = c("Max Age - 6.15myr", "Precise - 6.15myr"),
  Expected_Extinctions = c(round(expected_max_age, 5), round(expected_precise, 5)),
  Observed_Extinctions = rep(extinctions, 2),
  Ratio_Observed_Expected = c(round(extinctions / expected_max_age, 0), round(extinctions / expected_precise, 0))
)

kable(expected_extinctions, caption = "Expected vs Observed Extinctions") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
                full_width = FALSE, position = "center") %>%
  column_spec(1, bold = TRUE) %>%
  column_spec(4, bold = TRUE, color = "red")
```

Both approaches (comparing rates and number of extinctions) yield the same ratio / comparison.

### Comparison Table

```{r}
summary_comparison <- data.frame(
  Model = c("Max Age - 6.15myr", "Precise - 6.15myr"),
  Background_Rate_EMSY = c(background_rate_max_age_6.15myr, background_rate_precise_6.15myr),
  Current_Rate_EMSY = rep(round(extinctions_per_million_species_years, 1), 2),
  Instantaneous_Current_Rate = rep(round(instantaneous_emsy, 1), 2),
  Expected_Extinctions = c(paste0(round(expected_max_age, 5)), 
                          paste0(round(expected_precise, 5))),
  Observed_Extinctions = rep(extinctions, 2),
  Rate_Ratio_Direct = c(round(extinctions_per_million_species_years / background_rate_max_age_6.15myr, 0),
                         round(extinctions_per_million_species_years / background_rate_precise_6.15myr, 0)),
  Instantaneous_Rate_Increase = c(round(rate_increase_instant_max_age, 0), round(rate_increase_instant_precise, 0)),
  Extinction_Ratio_Counts = c(round(extinctions / expected_max_age, 0),
                               round(extinctions / expected_precise, 0)))

kable(summary_comparison,
      caption = "Complete Comparison: Rate vs Count Approaches",
      col.names = c("Model", "Background E/MSY", "Current E/MSY (Discrete)", "Current E/MSY (Instantaneous)", "Expected Extinctions*",
                    "Observed Extinctions", "Rate Ratio (Discrete)", "Rate Ratio (Instantaneous)", "Count Ratio")) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
                full_width = FALSE, position = "center") %>%
  column_spec(1, bold = TRUE) %>%
  column_spec(7:9, bold = TRUE, color = "red") %>%
  add_header_above(c(" " = 1, "Background Data" = 3, "Extinction Counts" = 2, "Magnitude of Increase" = 3)) %>%
  footnote(general = "*Expected extinctions calculated as: (Background E/MSY ÷ 1,000,000) × 101 species × 247 years")
```

Save excel

```{r}
# clean up column names
excel_data <- summary_comparison
names(excel_data) <- c("Model", "Background E/MSY", "Current E/MSY (Discrete)", "Current E/MSY (Instantaneous)", "Expected Extinctions*",
                    "Observed Extinctions", "Rate Ratio (Discrete)", "Rate Ratio (Instantaneous)", "Count Ratio")
# Save to Excel
write_xlsx(excel_data, "../outputs/DAISIE5_extinction_comparison_linear-and-exp.xlsx")

```
